blocks.text: Coquitlam West homes listed and sold, June to September 2026

Coquitlam West, September 2026. Detached houses: 76 listed at month end and 2 sold in September, a sales ratio of 3% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 359 listed at month end and 35 sold in September, a sales ratio of 10% (a buyers’ market).

On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 13 sold over 4 months against an average of 79.8 listed, about 24.5 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 6 sold. Condos and townhomes: 178 sold over 4 months against an average of 371.2 listed, about 8.3 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 55 sold.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Coquitlam West

items.t: Established-street house lots: single-detached streets under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, while apartment buildings cluster near the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations under the Transit-Oriented Areas framework.

Lot character from the zones: minimum lot size for subdivision is 650 m² with 18.5 m width for R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width for R-2, under Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. These are zone subdivision minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot are confirmed parcel by parcel (UNVERIFIED for any individual lot).

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam's SSMUH framework expressly leaves lots not connected to municipal water or sewer outside the SSMUH rules, which is the City's own servicing qualifier for house lots here; Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste. Parcel-level septic or well status is UNVERIFIED in the research — confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before pricing in added units.

ALR vs non-ALR: ALR status for the sub-area is UNVERIFIED in the research — no ALR parcel in Coquitlam West is confirmed and no ALR percentage split is stated. Check a specific parcel through the Agricultural Land Commission before applying any ALR rule.

Flood / watercourse position: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam, with Zoning Bylaw s.519 flood-protection setbacks and s.523 riparian rules behind it. A Fraser River floodplain designation for Coquitlam West's residential streets is UNVERIFIED.

Market context, labelled correctly: Coquitlam IS a SnapStats-covered community. SnapStats has NO land category, and no detached figure below is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Coquitlam West sub-area detached inventory 76 / solds 2 (3% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined 359 / 35 (10% ratio); Coquitlam community detached median $1,455,000 and combined condos & townhomes median $625,000. Sub-area medians are UNVERIFIED (community level only).
No bare-land strata plan in Coquitlam West was verified
Burquitlam Park District (Intergulf, Clarke Road and Como Lake Avenue) — PRESALE, documented as a proposal-stage development, never as lot inventory: It sells strata homes, not lots.

Southwest Shoulders and Corridors (adopted): the City's Transit-Oriented Areas Update and the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors review produced OCP and Zoning amendments creating medium-density housing and townhousing opportunities around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations and along Austin Avenue; the City states Council adopted the amendments following a public hearing. Whether a specific lot sits inside an amended area is a City confirmation for that parcel — the amendment map, not a listing claim, decides assembly value.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Coquitlam West

items.t: Coquitlam West is the City of Coquitlam's south-west side; the City plans the same ground as Southwest Coquitlam, covering the neighbourhoods around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre SkyTrain stations and along Austin Avenue. "Coquitlam West" is the GVR sub-area name in the SnapStats GVR September 2026 report. Exact sub-area boundary lines are UNVERIFIED — the City describes Southwest Coquitlam by its station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor, not by boundary roads.
Nearby areas: Central Coquitlam to the east, Maillardville to the south-east, Port Moody to the north-west, and Burnaby (Lougheed / Cariboo) across North Road to the west.

Main roads: North Road, Clarke Road, Austin Avenue and Lougheed Highway. Transit: Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines); per-route bus numbers are UNVERIFIED.

Civic anchors in this part of the city: Coquitlam Public Library Poirier branch, 575 Poirier Street (City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, serves Coquitlam as a whole); Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border — which hospital is closer for a specific address is UNVERIFIED.
Schools: School District 43 catchments are address-based and SD43 is a three-tier district. School names are Ministry-listed names only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Coquitlam West

items.t: Plan: the Interim Official Community Plan, Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026, supersedes OCP No. 3479. The adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments sit inside that framework for the station areas and Austin Avenue.

Watercourse diligence: a Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required within 30 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse, with Zoning Bylaw s.519 / s.523 setbacks — check slope and creek lots before pricing a split or an added unit.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Coquitlam West ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm-class thresholds are not documented in this area's own research, so no farm-class figure is asserted here. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

Coquitlam property taxes and utilities: City of Coquitlam property tax payment was due July 2, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants); utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste, and the City's 2026 budget materials record an average-household total property-charges increase of $137.

blocks.text: Good to know about Coquitlam West

items.t: Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026 (dated fact): the Interim Official Community Plan (Bylaws 5511/5512) was adopted April 27, 2026, superseding OCP No. 3479. Any page, listing package or assembly pitch still citing OCP No. 3479 as the current plan is out of date.

The townhouse supply story here is a planning document, not a building: the Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments were adopted to create townhousing opportunities around the two stations and Austin Avenue — the next named townhouse complexes in this sub-area will come from that amendment map, and a lot's position inside or outside it is the first diligence question on any "land value" pitch.

faq.q: Which SkyTrain stations serve Coquitlam West?
faq.a: Burquitlam Station (Millennium Line, Evergreen Extension) and Lougheed Town Centre Station (Millennium and Expo Lines); the City's Southwest Coquitlam planning is built around those two station areas and the Austin Avenue corridor.

faq.q: What sold in Coquitlam West in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 2 solds from 76 listings (3% sales ratio); condos & townhomes: 35 solds from 359 listings (10%). At the Coquitlam community level the detached median sale price was $1,455,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $625,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools serve a Coquitlam West address?
faq.a: School District 43 covers the area; for the sample address 575 Poirier Street, the SD43 locator result is Parkland Elementary, École Montgomery Middle and Centennial Secondary; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the locator.

faq.q: What planning change affects Coquitlam West houses?
faq.a: The adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors OCP and Zoning amendments, creating medium-density housing and townhousing opportunities around the Burquitlam and Lougheed Town Centre stations and along Austin Avenue, on top of the citywide SSMUH rules (up to 3–4 units on house lots).

faq.q: Is there a vacant lot subdivision I can buy into in Coquitlam West?
faq.a: No verified one — the area is established station-area strata plus interior house streets. Land trades as built house lots and assemblies, and no presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: How many homes can a house lot here carry under SSMUH?
faq.a: Up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes — and only where the lot is connected to municipal water and sewer; unserviced lots fall outside the rules.

faq.q: Does a lot near Burquitlam or Lougheed station carry redevelopment value?
faq.a: Possibly — the adopted Southwest Shoulders and Corridors amendments create medium-density and townhousing opportunities around both stations and along Austin Avenue. Whether the specific lot is inside an amended area is a City confirmation, not a listing claim.

faq.q: Is a Coquitlam West house lot serviced?
faq.a: The City's framework assumes municipal water and sewer for SSMUH eligibility and bills water, sewer/drainage and solid waste as City utilities — but parcel-level septic or well status is UNVERIFIED in the research, so confirm servicing for the specific lot with the City before writing.

faq.q: What servicing bylaw governs a subdivision here?
faq.a: The Subdivision and Development Servicing Bylaw No. 3558, 2003 — works and services must be provided to the City's standards under that bylaw, confirmed parcel by parcel with the City.
